record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: Draw studies of languages of finite words which are constructed by iterating prefix-suffix square completion, starting with spe- cial sets of initial words such as singleton sets, finite sets, regular sets, etc.

evidence.quote: Draw studies of languages of finite words which are constructed by iterating prefix-suffix square completion, starting with spe- cial sets of initial words such as singleton sets, finite sets, regular sets, etc.

artifact.status_search_result: Prefix-suffix square completion was introduced and several initial results (e.g., a linear-time decision procedure for the relation between two finite words, and the existence of infinite derivations avoiding repetitions of exponent > 2) are known. However, the broader program of classifying the iterated-completion languages obtained from singleton, finite, or regular initial sets does not appear to have been carried out in the literature; it is posed as a research direction rather than a settled theorem.

status_evidence.title: Prefix-Suffix Square Completion
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces the operation and studies derivations of infinite words; shows existence of words avoiding repetitions of exponent > 2 and gives a linear-time decision procedure for finite words.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational results exist but no general structural classification of iterated-completion languages from special initial sets.

status_evidence.title: Prefix–suffix square reduction
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the inverse (reduction) operation, indicating the area is actively investigated but the completion-based language classification remains open.
status_evidence.claim: Related operations are studied; the classification problem stated remains a research program.
